title: Canonical stationary comparisons along the bottom row
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $(E_r^{p,q},d_r)_{r\ge2}$ be a cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] indexed by $\mathbb Z^2$, with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and specified homology-to-next-page isomorphisms $e_r^{p,q}$. Assume $E_r^{p,q}=0$ for every $r\ge2$ whenever $p<0$ or $q\ne0$. At a bidegree $(p,q)$ form the short complex $E_r^{p-r,q+r-1}\to E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$; let $Z_r^{p,q}$ be the kernel of its outgoing differential, $i_r^{p,q}:Z_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p,q}$ its inclusion, and $\pi_r^{p,q}:Z_r^{p,q}\to\mathcal H(E_r)^{p,q}$ its homology quotient. For all $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ and $r\ge2$ with $r>\max(p,q+1)$, both adjacent differentials are zero, $i_r^{p,q}$ and $\pi_r^{p,q}$ are isomorphisms, and $t_r^{p,q}=e_r^{p,q}\circ\pi_r^{p,q}\circ(i_r^{p,q})^{-1}$ is a canonical isomorphism to $E_{r+1}^{p,q}$. Their iterated composites canonically identify all such late pages $E_r^{p,q}$, $r>\max(p,q+1)$, with one another. Moreover, for every $n\ge0$ the same conclusions about adjacent differentials, $i_r^{n,0}$, $\pi_r^{n,0}$ and $t_r^{n,0}$ hold for every $r\ge2$. The maps $a_{n,2}=1$ and $a_{n,r+1}=t_r^{n,0}\circ a_{n,r}$ are isomorphisms $E_2^{n,0}\to E_r^{n,0}$ for all $r\ge2$; at $r=n+2>\max(n,1)$ they identify $E_2^{n,0}$ with the stable bottom entry. For $n=0$, $a_{0,2}$ is the identity.

source.place: Tags 011N (definition-spectral-sequence), 011O (definition-limit-spectral-sequence) and 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness). Isolates old row-collapse Step 2, using all-page support as a hypothesis; no abutment is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $r\ge2$ and $(p,q)$. If $q\ne0$, the middle object $E_r^{p,q}$ is zero by hypothesis, so every morphism into or out of it is zero, by the defining uniqueness of morphisms to and from a zero object [def-sp-abelian]. If $q=0$, the incoming source has second coordinate $r-1>0$ and the outgoing target has second coordinate $1-r<0$; both are zero by the support hypothesis. Thus both adjacent differentials vanish at every bidegree for every $r\ge2$, in particular under the stated late-page bound.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-short-complex-zero-homology] to the short complex at $(p,q)$: the outgoing map is zero, so $i_r^{p,q}$ is an isomorphism; the incoming map is zero, so $\pi_r^{p,q}$ is an isomorphism. The specified $e_r^{p,q}$ is an isomorphism by [def-sp-spectral-sequence]. Consequently $t_r^{p,q}=e_r^{p,q}\circ\pi_r^{p,q}\circ(i_r^{p,q})^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $i_r^{p,q}\circ(\pi_r^{p,q})^{-1}\circ(e_r^{p,q})^{-1}$. This uses the canonical kernel inclusion and homology quotient of the item, so introduces no arbitrary isomorphism.

proof.text: For each bidegree define A_r from page two to page r by integer induction starting with A_2=1 and setting A_{r+1}=A_r followed by t_r. Define T_{r,s}=A_r^{-1} followed by A_s, restricting to the late pages in the conclusion. This is the forward finite composite for r≤s and its inverse for s<r: adjacent inverse factors cancel. The identities T_{r,r}=1 and T_{r,s} followed by T_{s,t}=T_{r,t} follow by associativity and the inverse identities, for arbitrary orders of pages. The recursion for A gives T_{r,r+1}=t_r, so its cycles square is the square from Step 2.

source.place: Tag 011N (definition-spectral-sequence), page homology; Tag 011O (definition-limit-spectral-sequence), degeneration and stationary identifications.

proof.text: For n≥0 put a(n,k)=A_{k+2} at bidegree (n,0). The base equation for the integer induction gives a(n,0)=1. Steps 1 and 2 give both zero differentials and the two isomorphism assertions on every page k+2. The recursion for A, cancellation of a(n,k) with its inverse, and the cycles square for t_{k+2} give the final required square. The integer n+2 is at least 2 and strictly exceeds both n and 1, so a(n,n) reaches a stable bottom entry; a(0,0) is the identity.
